meta.title: AI Governance & Architecture Review | Agentic Governance
meta.description: An AI governance and architecture review examines one agentic workflow — inputs, outputs, tool permissions, human approvals, cost per task — and delivers a control map, evaluation gaps, and a prioritized action plan.

title: Can you explain what the system did, how you evaluated it, and when a person steps in?
intro: Moving an AI assistant or agent into production raises three questions: what it may do, how its outputs are evaluated, and what it costs per completed task. We review one workflow end to end under your real operating conditions — and leave a control map and an action plan behind.

triggers.heading: Recognizable situations
items: A copilot or agent is moving from pilot to production and nobody has defined what it may do unsupervised.
LLM costs are growing faster than usage, and nobody can attribute spend to completed work.
Outputs look plausible in demos but hallucinate on the inputs your users actually send.

method.heading: How a review runs
method.intro: One workflow, traced end to end — same discipline as a number through a warehouse.
steps: Select one agentic workflow and the decision your team needs to make about it.
Examine inputs, outputs, tool permissions, human approval points, cost per completed task, and the traces available.
Run scenarios that reflect your actual operating conditions — not benchmark trivia.
Deliver a workflow and control map, observed evaluation gaps, a prioritized action plan, and a practical approach to monitoring cost and quality.

fields.label: Scenario
fields.text: An internal assistant drafts purchase requests: it reads a free-text request, looks up a supplier, fills the form fields, and can submit to the ERP.

fields.label: Human approval decision
fields.text: Any request above a defined amount, any new supplier, or any low-confidence field extraction requires a person before submission. Everything else can auto-submit with an audit trail.

fields.label: Output quality measure
fields.text: A request counts as valid when every extracted field matches the source and a reviewer would approve it without edits — measured on a weekly sample, not on a demo set.

fields.label: Model cost measure
fields.text: Model spend per accepted request — model spend divided by requests approved without correction, tracked per workflow so spend maps to completed work. When a full process cost is needed, the remaining measurable categories are scoped with you: infrastructure, tooling, rework, and human review time.

deliverables.heading: What you receive
items: A workflow and control map: which actions run autonomously, which require review, and why.
Observed evaluation gaps — where outputs are trusted but not verified.
A prioritized action plan for approvals, guardrails, and human checkpoints.
A practical monitoring plan for cost and output quality, plus architecture or local-first advice where the use case warrants it.

provides.heading: What we need from you
items: One workflow and a contact who can walk through it.
Access to representative traces, logs, or session exports — anonymized is fine.
The decision you are trying to make: ship, gate, redesign, or measure.

proof.heading: See the controls implemented
proof.text: Open ForceField — our open-source toolkit — implements several of the patterns this review recommends: prompt-injection detection, PII redaction, tool governance, and cost controls.

cta.heading: Discuss a review
cta.text: Scope is defined around a workflow, a deployment stage, and the decision your team needs to make. Email to start the conversation.
